To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C1d complex regulates the activity of specific isoforms of outer and inner dynein arms to produce wild-type motility.
the Pcdp1-C1d complex is essential for the proper coordination of dyneins in the cilia of Chlamydomonas.
Pcdp1 is required to coordinate the activity of dyenins in order to produce wild-type beating patterns in cilia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how cilia beat.
the mechanisms that regulate ciliary motility and how these mechanisms go awry in human disease.
the mechanisms that control ciliary motiity and the role of this motility in development and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
C1d regulates dynein activity by coordinating the activity of different dynein isoform.
Pcdp1 regulates the activity of dyenins and that it coordinates the activity of different isoforms.
the C1d complex coordinates the activity between outer and inner dynein arms to generate wild type ciliary motility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C1d regulates the activity of dyenein isoforms to coordinate microtubule bending and ciliary beating.
Pcdp1 and the C1d complex are required for wild-type cilia beating by coordinating the activity of dyenins isoforms.
the Pcdp1/ C1d complex coordinates the activity and/or distribution of dynein motors to produce wild-type beating cilia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C1d complex plays a unique role in coordinating the activity between different dynein isoform classes, which is essential for wild- type motility.
Pcdp1 is essential for wild type ciliary motility, and we have identified a mechanism by which Pcdp1 coordinates dynein isoform activity to produce the wild-type waveform.
the Pcdp1/ C1d complex plays a unique role in coordinating the activity between dynein arms to produce wild-type waveforms.
